title: Peak Expiratory Flow Trend in Asthma Exacerbation
scenario: A 14-year-old client with a history of asthma is admitted for an acute exacerbation. The nurse records peak expiratory flow (PEF) as a percentage of the client's personal best before and after each nebulized albuterol treatment.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Based on the overall flowsheet trend, how should the nurse interpret the client's response to treatment?

options.text: The client is improving and responding to therapy
The client is deteriorating and needs escalation
The client's status is unchanged since admission
The client is in impending respiratory failure

questions.rationale: Peak flow rising from 45% to 82% of personal best, a falling respiratory rate, improving oxygen saturation, clearing breath sounds, and resolving accessory muscle use together show a clear positive response to bronchodilator therapy.

questions.subject: Pediatrics
questions.stem: Which findings on the flowsheet support that the asthma exacerbation is improving? Select all that apply.

options.text: Peak flow increasing to 82% of personal best
SpO2 improving to 97% on room air
Wheezes present throughout expiration and inspiration

questions.rationale: Rising peak flow, a normalizing respiratory rate, improved oxygenation on room air, and loss of accessory muscle use all indicate improving airflow. Persistent widespread wheezing would suggest continued obstruction, not improvement.
